author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: I have reviewed the proposal for an automated validation layer. I will not approve moving to automated checks until the infrastructure costs are reduced to a level we can sustain. The current manual process is sufficient to manage the risk, and I am not willing to cross the line into automated infrastructure spending at this time. I am holding the process manual for now. If the costs remain high, I will refuse to sign off on any automated validation work. This is my firm position on the data pipeline architecture.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states a firm refusal to approve automated validation if costs remain high, defining a specific line that, if crossed, results in a refusal to sign off.
